title: Встреча с Родионом Сергеевичем на выкупе  (Meeting Rodion Sergeyevich at the Drop)

segments.t: Back at the kitchen, Max argues with Fedya about the contraband snails, while across town Kostya waits with Nastya's father at the ransom drop point. When homeless gentleman Rodion Sergeyevich walks up to collect the cash, Kostya cheerfully greets him by name.
А что ты меня вообще слушаешь?
А вы случайно пиво не пьете?
Родион Сергеевич, какое пиво зимой на улице?
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'Forgive me.' Max gently offers this polite apology for Fedya using "izvinite" ("excuse me") — the respectful form of "excuse me" or "sorry" used when stepping in or apologizing.
'They are perfectly fine.' Emphasizing how normal things are with Max, Fedya lands on "normalnyye" ("normal", built on "normalnyy") to keep the statement grounded.
'I just made an assumption.' Pushing back dryly in front of Fedya, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
А что ты меня вообще слушаешь?
'Why are you even listening to me in the first place?' Max inquires candidly whether Fedya really thought this through.
'And what if he does not show up?' Fedya cuts in firmly during the talk and puts the weight on "pridet" ("will come", from "priyti") as the exchange unfolds.
'He will show up, where else would he go?' Answering openly on the spot, the "-sya" ending on "denetsya" ("will go, get away") marks an action that unfolds mutually or turns back on the speaker.
'He needs the cash, which means he will show up.' Max steps in right away around Rodion, making his position completely clear.

'Konstantin, hello there.' Fedya simply extends this formal greeting at the start of the beat using "zdravstvuyte" ("hello") — the polite Russian greeting that literally wishes the other person good health.
А вы случайно пиво не пьете?
'Do you happen to drink beer, by any chance?' Holding firm candidly around Max, Rodion keeps normal statement word order here, turning the line into a question for Max purely through rising pitch.

'Hello, Rodion Sergeyevich.' Max calmly chooses this formal greeting in one quick breath using "zdravstvuyte" ("hello") — the polite Russian greeting that literally wishes the other person good health.
Родион Сергеевич, какое пиво зимой на улице?
'Rodion Sergeyevich, who drinks beer outside in the winter?' Mentioning the street on the spot, Fedya lands on "ulitse" ("street", built on "ulitsa") to keep the statement grounded.
'Well, one can see.' Turning quietly on the spot, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Tell me who your friend is.' Max inquires skeptically if there is more going on behind the scenes.
А что ты меня вообще слушаешь?
А вы случайно пиво не пьете?
Родион Сергеевич, какое пиво зимой на улице?

That wraps up this scene as max realizes the replacement snails are also questionable, while at the ransom drop Kostya accidentally ruins the handoff by greeting Rodion Sergeyevich by name. Until next time!
